items.title: 9.2.2 Key Parts of a Business Plan

source_refs.note: Topic 9.2.2 with the business-plan class activity (PDF 210-211, printed 207-209). The chai-dhaba business description is printed after the financial plan, out of order; the $100 example uses dollars. Short question 3 and long question 2 are answered.

blocks.caption: Key parts of a business plan
rows: Executive summary
a brief overview: what the business does, its goals and how
the most important points in short
Business description
products or services, target customers, what is unique
a chai dhaba with freshly brewed chai near the bazaar
Market analysis
customers, their needs and competitors
pet owners and other pet-sitting services nearby
Organization and management
how the business is organized; team and roles
a school club's president and secretary
Products or services
features and benefits
how tutoring lessons raise grades
Marketing and sales strategy
how to attract and keep customers
a crafts business using social media and local fairs
Financial plan
budget, funding needs and expected revenue
how to raise money for supplies and what it will earn

blocks.alt: Left: five boxes in a cycle, Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype and Test, each with a school-bag example, and a red arrow from Test back to Empathize. Right: seven boxes for the parts of a business plan with short notes. Bottom: five pitch steps, problem, solution, unique point, audience and questions, using a juice shop.
blocks.caption: Design thinking, the business plan and the pitch (original diagram after topics 9.1 to 9.3).
blocks.long_description: Design thinking starts by empathizing with users, such as asking students about their bags, then defines the problem (a light, strong, roomy bag), ideates solutions (padding, pockets), builds a quick prototype (a cardboard model) and tests it with users; their feedback loops back to improve the design. A business plan covers the executive summary, business description, market analysis, organization and management, products or services, marketing and sales, and the financial plan. A pitch states the problem, the solution, what makes it unique and who it is for, and prepares for questions.

blocks.prompt: Class activity: write a business plan for a simple idea such as a school bake sale, using these parts (plus an appendix if needed), then share it and give feedback. List the key steps (short question 3) and explain why each is critical (long question 2).
blocks.explanation: Steps: define the idea and summarize it; describe the business; analyse the market; set out the team; detail the products; plan marketing and sales; prepare the financial plan. Each matters: the summary convinces readers quickly; the description and products make the offer clear; market analysis shows real demand and competitors; the team shows who will do the work; marketing explains how customers will be found; and the financial plan shows whether the business can pay for itself and how much money is needed.

items: Seven parts: summary, description, market, organization, products, marketing and sales, finance.
